messages:
nina: Quick heads-up — hit OOM + race during onboarding of a 30B safetensors bundle. Partial shard hotplug raced with two warmup workers; one started KV cache population, other nuked it. We lost requests for ~30s. Putting a brief design ask here.

omar: ugh. any logs / stack traces?

nina: paste
```
2026-03-18T12:03:21Z ERROR warmup_manager: failed to apply shard-lease: CAS failed
2026-03-18T12:03:21Z WARN shard_loader: started warmup for shard s-7f8 but eviction in-flight
2026-03-18T12:03:22Z ERROR inference: OOM while allocating activation buffer for layer 12
```

li: idea: introduce a transient lease token for shard-onboarding. When a worker starts warmup it CASes a lease key in our registry with TTL and worker-id. Other workers must observe lease and either join as helper or backoff. If lease expires, next worker can take over. This avoids double-warmup / conflicting eviction.

jade: how do we guarantee atomicity across registry failures? etcd flakiness caused similar split-brain in canaries.

li: use compare-and-swap against the checkpoint namespace (we already do CAS for manifest uploads). Fallback: local advisory lock + manifest-first path that streams but avoids in-place write. Also add a short-lived on-disk temp-file marker so eviction sees 'in progress' and won't remove.

nina: ps — safetensors gotchas: header parsing is cheap but we stream chunked shards; we sometimes mis-detect alignment which made warmup re-read headers mid-stream. header-first check would help.

omar: telemetry? what metrics needed to reason about this in prod?

nina: suggested metrics:
- shard_warmup_attempts_total
- shard_warmup_concurrent_workers
- shard_lease_acquire_latency
- shard_lease_conflicts_total
- shard_warmup_time_seconds
- shard_premature_eviction_count

warmup-bot: [alert] instance i-0a3 warmup latency spike 2026-03-18T12:04:00Z -> 68s

jade: what about safetensors-specific checksum to detect partial reads? add 64-bit header checksum in bundle metadata so streaming readers validate first chunk and bail early.

li: alternatively we can fetch first 16KB (header+toc) via range request and validate, then proceed streaming for weights. This saves signature ops and avoids full-mmap until successful.

omar: operationally, I'd add a feature flag for 'transient-lease' and run on Dedicated canaries first.

nina: agreed. follow-up action: I'll open an RFC/PR with design: lease + in-progress marker + header-range prefetch + metrics. Tagging @li @omar @jade for review. :+1:

jade: ack. also add a fallback plan to manifest-first streaming for any lease failures.

li: ack. will sketch the registry CAS snippet:
```
# pseudo
if cas(registry, key, expected=null, value={worker:W, ts:now, ttl:30s}):
  // we own lease
else:
  // helper/backoff
```

omar: cool. nina — ping when RFC/PR exists and I'll schedule canary runs.

nina: will do. thanks folks. :rocket:
